summary: 'I don't think they are the same.' sent right after an unrelated 2-file CSV comparison (which itself followed a service-code comparison two turns earlier) was resolved against the file comparison alone, never considering the service-code claim it most plausibly meant.
preconditions: Conversation: 'What is the difference between F-Line and F-Line Appeal?' -> both codes explained. 'Compare the service codes in both files.' -> deterministic 2-file comparison table. Then the correction.
reproduction: 1. Ask the F-Line/F-Line Appeal comparison question.
2. Ask an unrelated file comparison question.
3. Send: 'I don't think they are the same.'

Before fix: 'You have 2 files attached in this session... Which one do you mean?' -- defaulted to the file topic because `attachment_qa.plan_answer()` claims any negative correction unconditionally whenever `attachment_topic_active()` reads True, with no awareness of the earlier, equally plausible service-code claim.
expected: Per the task's own requirement: 'Determine whether this refers to the two services or the file comparison. If the wording does not establish which claim is disputed, ask a focused clarification that names the plausible alternatives. Do not automatically select the latest file-related topic.'
actual_before_fix: Silently defaulted to the file-disambiguation question, never surfacing the F-Line/F-Line Appeal claim as a candidate at all.
root_cause: `attachment_qa.plan_answer()`'s negative-correction gate only checks `attachment_topic_active(db, session_id)` (whether the SINGLE most recent assistant turn was about a file) -- it never looks further back in the conversation for a competing, non-attachment claim the correction might actually mean.
verified_outcome: Live UI, fresh conversation, 2026-10-13 ~16:48: the same 3-turn setup, then 'I don't think they are the same.' -> 'Understood -- it's not clear which answer you mean: the uploaded file(s), or the service-code comparison you just asked about? Let me know which one, and I'll re-check it.' Fix: new `_route_negative_correction()` in backend/services/chatbot.py, called before the attachment layer, scans the last 3 assistant turns for a plausible non-attachment claim (service code / application / field visit) and asks a named, two-option clarification when both an active attachment topic AND a recent non-attachment claim are plausible and the message gives no cue either way. Regression: none (new function; unit-tested directly, no DB needed for the pure routing decision).
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, 2026-10-13 ~16:48

summary: 'I don't think the files have the same service codes.' (requirement C -- an UNAMBIGUOUS file-scoped correction, since 'the files' is the grammatical subject) was read as equally ambiguous between file and service-code, because the message happens to also contain the words 'service codes'.
preconditions: Same conversation as FLINE-NEGATION-001a, sent as the very next message after the model's own ambiguous clarification.
reproduction: Send: 'I don't think the files have the same service codes.' right after the ambiguous clarification from FLINE-NEGATION-001a.

First fix attempt: fell to the GENERIC 'I may have misunderstood' fallback -- neither the file-aware nor the service-code-aware handler, because the message matched BOTH the file-cue and the service-cue regex simultaneously, and the symmetric 'explicit_file and not explicit_service' / 'explicit_service and not explicit_file' test satisfied neither.
expected: Recheck the file comparison specifically, per the task's own requirement C ('Recheck the file comparison, not the service-code definitions.')
actual_before_fix: A generic, topic-blind 'misunderstood' message that referenced neither files nor service codes.
root_cause: The explicit-cue check in `_route_negative_correction()` treated 'files' and 'service codes' as two EQUALLY-WEIGHTED, mutually exclusive signals; a sentence naming both (because 'service codes' is the grammatical ATTRIBUTE of 'the files', not a second competing claim) satisfied neither of the two one-sided conditions and fell through unresolved.
verified_outcome: Live UI, 2026-10-13 ~16:48 (first fix attempt) confirmed the gap; second fix (`_NEGCORR_FILE_SUBJECT_RE`, a pattern recognising '(the) files ... have/contain/share/match/carry ...' as file-subject phrasing, checked before the symmetric cue test) resolves the message to the attachment route outright. Verified unit-level (3/3 scenario checks) and live (see FLINE-NEGATION-001c for the full live re-test after the second and third fixes combined).

summary: Two further bugs found while fixing FLINE-NEGATION-001b, both now fixed: (1) the router correctly said 'attachment' but the underlying handler still declined because `attachment_topic_active()`'s single-last-turn read had been reset by the router's OWN prior ambiguous-clarification turn; (2) once reached, the 2-file-comparison case still defaulted to 'which file do you mean?' instead of rechecking the comparison.
reproduction: After the _NEGCORR_FILE_SUBJECT_RE fix alone: 'I don't think the files have the same service codes.' -> still 'You have 2 files attached in this session... Which one do you mean?' -- the router correctly chose 'attachment', but `attachment_qa.plan_answer()`'s OWN re-derivation of `attachment_topic_active()` read False (because the immediately preceding turn was the router's own ambiguous-clarification reply, saved with no attachment structured_data), so it declined and fell through to the unrelated generic handler.

After routing to `_handle_negative_correction()` directly (bypassing the stale re-check): now reached the function, but with 2 documents attached and no single 'focused' document (a 2-file comparison leaves no single focus by design), it defaulted to 'Which one do you mean?' -- the wrong question for a claim about the comparison across BOTH files.
expected: Recheck the specific prior comparison between the two named files, not re-derive stale attachment-active state and not ask which SINGLE file is meant for a claim that was never about just one.
actual_before_fix: Fell through to the unrelated 'I may have misunderstood...' generic handler (bug 1), then 'Which one do you mean?' (bug 2).
root_cause: (1) `attachment_qa.plan_answer()`'s own gate always re-derives `attachment_topic_active()` from the single most recent assistant turn, independent of and redundant with `_route_negative_correction()`'s own, more informed decision. (2) `_handle_negative_correction()`'s `len(docs) > 1` branch had no case for 'the last answer itself spanned multiple documents' -- only 'exactly one focused document' or 'ask which one'.
verified_outcome: Live UI, fresh conversation, 2026-10-13 ~17:02: full 4-turn sequence (F-Line Appeal comparison -> file comparison -> ambiguous correction -> explicit file correction) all resolve correctly, ending in: 'Understood -- let me recheck the comparison between sis_svccode_fileB.csv and sis_svccode_fileA.csv. Name the specific service code or row you think is wrong, or I'll show the full comparison again.' Fixes: (1) the router's 'ambiguous' response now carries forward the PRIOR attachment context's document_ids as its own saved structured_context, instead of None, so the next turn's lookup still finds the right file set; (2) chatbot.py's negative-correction call sites, when the router says 'attachment', now call `attachment_qa._handle_negative_correction()` directly (fetching documents fresh) instead of going back through `plan_answer()`'s own, now-redundant and occasionally stale topic-active gate; (3) `_handle_negative_correction()` gained a 'the previous answer spanned multiple documents' branch that re-targets all of them and offers to recheck the comparison, checked before the generic 'which file' fallback.
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, 2026-10-13 ~16:48-17:02 (iterative fix-and-reverify)

summary: Several of the task's own required negative-correction test phrases were not recognised as corrections at all by `is_negative_correction()`, so neither the attachment-side nor the general-side handler ever ran for them -- they fell through as ordinary (unparseable) questions.
preconditions: No upload needed for most of these.
reproduction: "I don't think they are the same." -> False (before fix)
"I don't think the files have the same service codes." -> False (before fix)
"I don't think the F-Line and F-Line Appeal definitions are correct." -> False (before fix)
expected: All four recognised as negative corrections, per the task's explicit test list (section 2: 'not that', 'wrong answer', "that's incorrect", 'I meant the other one', "I don't think that's correct", and the Conversation A-D phrasings).
actual_before_fix: `_NEGATIVE_CORRECTION_RE` only matched the EXACT phrase 'I don't think so' / "I don't think that's correct" -- not the general shape 'I don't think <subject> <verb>', and had no bare "that's incorrect" alternative at all (only 'that's wrong' / 'not ... right/correct' variants).
root_cause: backend/services/attachment_qa.py `_NEGATIVE_CORRECTION_RE`, too narrow a set of fixed phrases for the disagreement-sentence shapes this task's own test matrix requires.
verified_outcome: Fixed by adding a bounded general pattern `i don't think (<=6 words> is|are|was|were|have|has|match(es)?)` (hyphen-aware, so 'F-Line' survives as one token) and a bare "that's incorrect" alternative. Re-verified against a 13-case matrix including negative controls (ordinary SIS questions that must NOT match) -- all pass. Not independently re-tested live beyond the cases already covered by FLINE-NEGATION-001a/b/c and the live F-Line Appeal/CSV re-verification, since this is a pure classification regex with its own unit coverage.
evidence_source: direct `is_negative_correction()` calls, 2026-10-13 ~16:46; full regression suite re-run clean (see SIS_Context_And_PostUpload_Regression_Results.csv)

summary: The prior pass's fix for ATTACH-INTERCEPT-001 was scoped to exactly one intent (service_code_lookup); per this task's instruction, it is now generalized to EVERY deterministic intent, matching the rule `targets_attachment()` itself already uses (claim a turn only on `general_query`).
preconditions: A file attached; the first (or any) question after upload that the deterministic intent parser resolves to something other than general_query.
reproduction: Before this generalization (but after the prior pass's narrow fix): only `service_code_lookup` was exempted from the attachment-topic-active fallback; any OTHER deterministic intent asked as the first message after an upload was still at risk of being wrongly routed through the attachment evidence path, per the prior pass's own stated limitation.

Live spot-checks this pass found 'What is my workload?' and 'What is UDS?' already worked correctly as first-messages-after-upload BEFORE this change -- both are protected by other, pre-existing guards (`_is_register_shaped()` for workload-style DB queries; the `_merge_turn` pre-pipeline handler, which runs before the attachment layer at all, for UDS). This does not mean the narrow fix was sufficient in general -- it means the specific intents spot-checked happened to already be covered by unrelated mechanisms; the task's own instruction (not to rely on a growing one-off list) was followed regardless.
expected: No deterministic intent should need its own individual exemption; the SAME condition `targets_attachment()` uses to decide whether to even consider the attachment (general_query vs. not) should govern this fallback too.
actual_before_this_change: `intent == 'service_code_lookup'` was the only exemption -- correct for the confirmed case, but a maintenance trap: every NEW deterministic intent added to the parser in the future would need its own line added here or silently inherit the same exposure.
root_cause: backend/services/attachment_qa.py `plan_answer()`'s topic-active fallback used a single-intent exemption instead of mirroring `targets_attachment()`'s own general_query rule.
verified_outcome: Live UI, 2026-10-13 ~17:03: 'Which applications are overdue?' (officer_workload-family intent) asked as the FIRST message after an upload answers correctly from the database, immediately followed in the same conversation by 'What is F-Line Appeal?' (0185, correct) and 'List all the service codes in this file.' (deterministic, correct) -- all three intents coexist correctly in one session. Full attachment regression suite (10 suites, 199 checks) re-run clean against the broadened condition `intent != "general_query"`.
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, 2026-10-13 ~17:03; SIS_Context_And_PostUpload_Regression_Results.csv

summary: The task's section 3 requests a full 6-condition x many-intent-category matrix (service-code definitions, F-Line/F-Line Appeal, glossary, workflow/procedure, application-status, application-detail, field visits, fee queries, workload, DB-backed queries, uploaded-document questions, file relevance, CSV column/row ops, multi-file comparisons, and 'other deterministic intents found in the routing implementation'). This pass spot-checked 2 categories (workload/overdue-listing, a glossary term) in addition to the 3 directly-confirmed defects (service-code lookup, F-Line Appeal comparison, CSV enumeration) and verified the generalized fix via code review of the single condition it now shares with `targets_attachment()`. It did NOT individually re-verify every remaining category live.
root_cause: n/a -- time/scope, not a defect. The generalization (intent != general_query) is a single code path shared by every deterministic intent, so it is not expected to behave differently per intent category; this is architectural confidence, not per-category live verification, and is reported as such rather than claimed as exhaustive testing.
verified_outcome: NOT independently verified per-category. The two categories spot-checked (workload/overdue, UDS glossary) both passed. Field visits, fee queries, application-detail, file-relevance and multi-file-comparison-as-first-question-after-upload were not individually re-tested this pass.
